text: TYPHOON PEDRING NESAT DEVASTATED METRO MANILA CENTRAL AND NORTHERN LUZON On This Day September 27 2011 Typhoon Pedring PH International Name NESAT carved a path of catastrophic destruction across the Philippines when it made landfall on September 27 2011 As a powerful Category 4 equivalent typhoon it unleashed ferocious maximum sustained winds of 215 km/h and dropped torrents of relentless rain that quickly overwhelmed Luzon The immense storm triggered widespread landslips brought down vital electrical grids and forced hundreds of thousands of residents to abandon their homes for safety The sheer volume of water forced major dams to open their spillway gates significantly aggravating the downstream flooding in neighboring northern provinces In Metro Manila the storm brought the nation's capital to a complete standstill evoking terrifying memories of Tropical Storm Ondoy PH from two years prior Strong gales combined with an exceptionally high storm surge generated massive 20 foot waves that breached the historic seawall along Roxas Boulevard The resulting saltwater deluge swamped key arterial roads the United States Embassy and the iconic five-star Sofitel Philippine Plaza hotel Meanwhile low lying sectors like Marikina experienced critical flooding as local rivers swelled to dangerous levels trapping families on rooftops and necessitating emergency rubber boat rescues The aftermath of Typhoon PEDRING left behind a staggering socioeconomic toll claiming 85 lives in the Philippines alone and leaving billions of pesos in property damage Central and Northern Luzon's expansive agricultural fields-the backbone of the country's rice supply suffered heavily with massive swathes of crops entirely wiped out by the standing floodwaters Compounding the humanitarian crisis communities like Calumpit and Hagonoy in Bulacan remained submerged in chest-deep water for days without clean electricity or drinking water The disaster forced a declaration of a state of calamity across Luzon marking PEDRING as one of the most economically devastating typhoons of its time Philippine Weather Disturbances 27 September 2026 Pedring2011 Typhoon Pedring NESAT2011 text: THE RAIN IS NATURAL THE SUFFERING ISN'T Metro Manila is flooding again today Roads in several cities have been flooded some becoming impassable while La Mesa Dam reached spilling level and residents along the Tullahan River were told to evacuate And we hear a familiar explanation The rain was simply too strong Climate change is real The weather is becoming more extreme Nature cannot be controlled All of that is true But it can also become a very convenient excuse Government cannot stop the rain It can decide whether drainage systems work whether waterways are kept clear whether pumping stations are maintained whether watersheds are protected and whether billions spent on flood control actually produce flood control The President himself acknowledged that some flood-control projects in Bulacan were never built His administration is still investigating projects alleged to be ghost substandard or ineffective So yes blame the rain for falling But don't blame the rain for money disappearing Don't blame climate change for a ghost project Don't blame nature for poor planning And don't ask people standing in waist-deep water to accept government failure as an act of God Other countries face nature too Singapore lives with intense tropical rainfall In the 1960s and 1970s it suffered widespread flooding Decades of drainage expansion detention systems strict building rules maintenance and careful planning reduced its officially identified flood-prone area from around 3,200 hectares to less than 30 hectares today Japan cannot prevent earthquakes Yet it prepares buildings infrastructure evacuation systems and communities for them Around Tokyo Japan built one of the world's largest underground flood channels to divert overflowing rivers and reduce flood damage They did not defeat nature They prepared for it We have not lacked money in our country We have spent enormous sums on flood-control projects Yet we are now dealing with a major corruption scandal involving precisely those projects People pay taxes for protection from floods Money is allocated for that protection Then the rains come and families lose appliances cars businesses school days Lives And afterward they are told Malakas kasi ang ulan Of course the rain was strong That was the reason to prepare No serious engineer can promise a flood-free Metro Manila Even Singapore still experiences flash floods Climate change is making the problem harder The proper measure of government is whether flooding becomes less frequent less deep shorter more predictable and less deadly That requires drainage maps watershed management zoning enforcement retention basins sewer maintenance pumping capacity garbage collection engineering standards long-term budgets and COMPETENT people allowed to do their jobs It also requires public money actually reaching the project for which it was intended Nature will always test a country The rain will fall on an honest government and a corrupt government alike The difference is what happens after the rain reaches the ground If another generation of Filipinos is still wading through the same streets after billions more have been spent we should ask what exactly our leaders have been building while the rest of the Filipinos were paying for it Teach Better

text: DOST PAGASA inaugurates JICA funded CDO River Basin Flood Forecasting and Warning System DOST-PAGASA has inaugurated the Cagayan De Oro River Basin Flood Forecasting and Warning System FFWS today at the PAGASA Mindanao Regional Services Division in El Salvador City Misamis Oriental This facility aims to provide early warning and real-time monitoring for flood-prone communities in Misamis Oriental and some parts of Bukidnon enhancing disaster preparedness in the region Funded by the Government of Japan through the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA this system features an enhanced flood forecasting and warning including additional telemetered and sturdier rainfall and water level monitoring stations along with X-Band radars These strategically positioned stations spanning from the upstream to downstream sections of the river basin will enable hydrologists at the CDORBFFWS to provide accurate timely and relevant flood bulletins and warnings to communities vulnerable to flooding DOST officials graced the event with Secretary Renato U Solidum Jr as the inaugural speaker Also in support and attendance are DOST Undersecretary for Regional Operations Engr Sancho A Mabborang and PAGASA Administrator Dr Nathaniel T Servando Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan His Excellency Kazuya Endo and Senior Representative of JICA Mr Morishima Takanori also attended the event delivering messages of support Local Chief Executives and representatives of involved LGUs partner agencies stakeholders and many officials also gathered for the inauguration receiving plaques of appreciation The launching event featured a blessing ceremony unveiling of the marker ribbon-cutting facility tour and a press conference CDO River Basin One DOST4U Science For The People PAGASA Flood Warning DOST Bukidnon DOST Camiguin DOST Lanao del Norte DOST Misamis Occidental DOST Misamis Oriental

text: DAVAO CITY DELIVERS RELIEF TO FLOOD-HIT FAMILIES IN TALOMO MUSLIM VILLAGE The City Government of Davao through the Davao City Muslim Affairs Office conducted a relief distribution for flood-affected families in the Maguindanaon Community of Barangay Talomo Muslim Village Representing the Maguindanaon and Tausug Tribes the humanitarian effort was led by Deputy Edyamein Ahalul of the Tausug Tribe and Deputy Gabriel Nakan of the Maguindanaon Tribe Food and grocery packs were distributed to families impacted by the recent flooding as part of the city's continuing disaster response The organizers expressed their gratitude to Davao City Mayor Sebastian Baste Duterte for his continued support of the city's Muslim communities They also acknowledged the generosity of private sponsors and partner Panadero Bakeshop for helping make the relief operation possible The initiative highlights the importance of collaboration between the local government private organizations and community leaders in providing timely assistance to Dabawenyos affected by natural disasters Dabawenews

text: THE BLUEPRINT FOR FLOOD CONTROL MASTERPLAN IS READY The recent post by FB page More of Davao has reignited an important conversation-Davao City's flooding problem is not due to the absence of a plan In fact one already exists The Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA in partnership with the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH completed the Project for Master Plan and Feasibility Study on Flood Control and Drainage in Davao City in July 2023 after several years of technical studies and consultations The project itself commenced in November 2018 following the signing of the Record of Discussions in April 2018 between JICA and the Philippine government The completed master plan is comprehensive It covers the Davao Matina and Talomo River Basins and recommends a combination of structural measures including river dredging cut-off channels retarding ponds retarding basins and drainage improvements to significantly reduce flood risks in the city These are not theoretical concepts They are the product of years of hydrological studies engineering surveys and technical analysis by Filipino and Japanese experts This is why the public deserves to know one thing what is the current status of implementation Large Official Development Assistance ODA infrastructure projects commonly undergo additional stages that include financing arrangements detailed engineering environmental compliance right-of-way acquisition and government approvals before actual construction begins That does not diminish the urgency Every flooding incident reminds us that studies alone cannot protect lives Master plans only become meaningful once construction begins The engineering has already been completed The science has already been established The blueprint already exists The next chapter should no longer be about producing another report It should be about turning years of planning into flood control infrastructure that protects communities businesses and lives Because when it comes to flooding what Davaoeños need most is not another promise-they need progress backed by action

text: READ Collapsed Callawa Bridge part of 2017 DPWH Project A bridge in Purok 2 Barangay Callawa Buhangin Davao City collapsed following heavy rains and flooding since Monday night disrupting access for residents and motorists in the area Photos circulating on social media showed portions of the bridge giving way as strong floodwaters battered the creek below amid continuous downpour Documents shared with the media identified the structure as part of a Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH project under Contract ID 17LO 0133 for the Concreting/Widening/Improvement of Bypass Road at Buhangin-Tigatto-Mandug-Callawa-Fatima Road including Reconstruction of Callawa Bridge and RROW in Davao City's 2nd District The contract was signed on May 11 2017 during the term of then Davao City 2nd District Representative Vincent Garcia and awarded by DPWH Region 11 to Premium Megastructures Inc with a total contract cost of P184,588,193.30 and a completion period of 240 calendar days The agreement was signed on behalf of the government by then DPWH 11 OIC-Regional Director Allan Borromeo DPWH 11 spokesperson Dean Ortiz said the approximately 15 meter bridge had been affected by worsening erosion over the years due to the widening of the creek beneath it which was further aggravated by continuous heavy rains and strong flood currents since Monday night The creek widened significantly over the years eroding the bridge approaches until the structure could no longer withstand the pressure from the floodwaters Ortiz said No injuries or casualties were reported Authorities are assessing the damage and monitoring other flood-affected areas in Davao City Contributed photos

text: Flood in Obrero 1960s I am taking a quick break from my work Speaking of the heavy flood it reminds me of something Here is a photo of some residents in Obrero at the corner of Clarin and Porras Streets during the flood This photo comes from the contributor's grandmother's family album The scene was possibly taken in the 1960s We learn from historian Antonio Figueroa that Barrio Obrero had its beginnings in the pre-Commonwealth period The idea was to set aside parcels of land to be developed into villages for working men And let me tell you a collective memory from my personal journal about Obrero's surrounding areas In old maps of Davao the area from Trading Boulevard Sta Ana Agdao all the way to Obrero was a swampy or marshy and mangrove area In fact in Ubalde and R Castillo roads there were plenty of Pagatpat trees At high tide seawater would come in bringing with it fish like ibis bugaong wild tilapia and the water snake called tangkig Of course there were also crabs like kuray katang and alimango In Obrero alone sometime in the past some college students who stayed in boarding houses fondly recalled how they would put their shoes in a basin floating in dirty water so they could wear them the next morning I wonder how many parts of the city have still experienced flooding since the 1960s or even earlier I want to learn from urban planners And the two young men from the right They are so wet in the rain Neil Teves Author's note Photo courtesy of the Bonifacio and Ermitania Delute Family Albums Contributed by Neil Gementiza Photo first posted by Paul Corpus on November 2 2019 for educational purposes

text: Flood Control gusto Budget Allocation ayaw Under the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program NEP the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH Region XI received only PHP 2.024 billion for flood control projects Compared to other regions with similar populations land areas and flood risks this is among the lowest allocations nationwide Of this PHP 2.024 billion Davao City was earmarked just a single listed project worth PHP 217 million with no mention of the JICA-assisted Flood Control Master Plan It should be noted that during his recent visit President Ferdinand Marcos Jr stated that the administration would revisit the master plan to address the city's recurring flooding issues Nationwide the Philippine government has earmarked PHP 107.4 billion for flood control projects under the proposed 2027 NEP covering both nationally funded and foreign-assisted initiatives

text: BACKHOE NI CONG DANNY DOMINGO NASA BRGY SAN PABLO HAGONOY PARA SA PAGSASAAYOS NG PILAPIL LABAN SA BAHA Ni Marcel Bayan MCB NewsTV Bistado ng Bayan HAGONOY Bulacan Nasa Barangay San Pablo na ang backhoe na ipinadala ni Congressman Danny A Domingo bilang tugon sa kahilingan ng mga opisyal ng barangay na maisara ang mga nabutas na bahagi ng pilapil ng mga palaisdaan na pinaniniwalaang nagiging daanan ng tubig at nag-aambag sa pagbaha sa mga Barangay San Pablo at San Pedro sa Hagonoy Bulacan Ayon sa mga opisyal ng Barangay San Pablo layunin ng hakbang na ito na maisara ang mga butas sa mga pilapil na pinapasukan at dinadaluyan ng tubig na maaaring magpalala sa pagbaha sa mga nasabing lugar Umaasa ang mga residente ng San Pablo at San Pedro na sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng backhoe at pagsasagawa ng kaukulang pagsasaayos ay mababawasan ang pagpasok ng tubig sa mga lugar na madalas maapektuhan ng pagbaha Nagpaabot naman ng taos-pusong pasasalamat ang mga opisyal ng Barangay San Pablo kay Cong Danny A Domingo o mas kilala bilang Cong DAD sa agarang pagtugon sa kanilang pangangailangan Pinasalamatan din nila si Sir Didis Domingo at si Sir Jem Castro ng tanggapan ng kongresista sa Unang Distrito ng Bulacan sa pagtulong upang maisakatuparan ang nasabing hakbang Para sa mga residente mahalagang bahagi ng pagsisikap na maibsan ang pagbaha ang pagtutulungan ng mga lokal na opisyal at mga kinatawan ng pamahalaan lalo na sa mga lugar na patuloy na nahaharap sa problema ng pag-apaw at pagpasok ng tubig Inaasahan ng mga mamamayan na ang pagsasaayos ng mga nabutas na pilapil ay makatutulong sa pagpapabuti ng kondisyon sa Barangay San Pablo at San Pedro habang patuloy na isinusulong ang iba pang mga hakbang upang matugunan ang suliranin sa pagbaha

text: THE HOSTAGE BLUEPRINT JICA MASTERPLAN FOR DAVAO CITY What if I told you that a blueprint to stop the flooding in Davao City is already finished It was designed by some of the best engineers in the world printed and is currently sitting on a desk in Manila Here is the truth about the JICA Master Plan the political war currently holding it hostage and what our Local Government Unit LGU is doing to keep our heads above water while we wait The Real Solution The JICA Master Plan Back in 2018 the Philippine government partnered with the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA to solve our city's flooding Instead of just building basic concrete walls which easily overflow the Japanese and local engineers designed a massive city-wide system The core of the plan involves digging massive retarding basins giant empty catch-ponds built in the uplands When a storm hits millions of gallons of water would flow into these basins and be held there safely trapping the water before it ever reaches barangays like Ma-a Matina and Talomo It is brilliant it is proven and it is ready But just look at the timeline of how it got stuck in politics Here is the timeline April 2019 THE STUDY BEGINS The Philippine government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA sign an agreement to create a long-term multi-basin master plan 2018-2022 WHY WASN'T IT BUILT UNDER DUTERTE A common question is why this wasn't funded during former President Rodrigo Duterte's term The answer is engineering reality The Japanese engineers were still studying our rivers You cannot fund or construct a mega-project when the architects haven't finished the blueprints July 2023 THE BLUEPRINT IS FINISHED JICA officially completes the Master Plan Instead of basic walls it proposes PHP 41.7 Billion to build massive retarding basins giant empty bowls upstream to catch and hold storm water before it hits our urban barangays AUGUST 9 2024 VP SARA CALLS OUT THE MISSING BUDGET Vice President Sara Duterte issues a strong public statement pointing out the lack of government action She calls out the current administration for refusing to fund the finalized master plan questioning if the budget is being intentionally withheld simply because the sitting mayor is a Duterte Baka naman may alinlangan pa hinggil dito dahil Duterte ang mayor at mas mamarapatin nilang gibain na lang she stated 2025 Present STILL WAITING FOR FUNDS Despite the blueprint being ready for over two years the national government has still not released the funding needed to actually build it Bureaucracy or Sabotage While politicians debate whether the delay is just standard government red tape for a foreign loan or a deliberate political attack to damage the Duterte family ordinary Davaoeños are the collateral damage We are the ones sweeping mud out of our homes The ultimate solution to our flooding is being treated as a political football What is the LGU Doing While We Wait The Davao City local government cannot afford a PHP 41.7 Billion mega-project on its own They cannot single-handedly buy multi-hectare lands to build giant retarding ponds without national funding However they are not just sitting around waiting for our government Without the big blueprint the LGU is focusing heavily on immediate urban drainage nature-based mitigation and survival Here is what the city is doing right now Aggressive Drainage and Inlet Upgrades The City Engineer's Office CEO and Task Force Drainage are continuously ripping up flood-prone choke points In 2025 alone they funded five new major inlet projects to help water subside faster on critical roads like Diversion Road fronting Panacan Cemetery Quezon Boulevard and Cabantian-Bunawan Preventing Blockages The city's Ancillary Services Unit ASU is conducting aggressive year-round desilting and garbage clearing of these new drainage systems so the street-level water actually has somewhere to go Smart Early Warning Systems If the LGU cannot completely stop the water they focus on keeping people alive Davao City relies heavily on its high-definition river cameras monitoring the Talomo Matina and Davao rivers 24/7 This real-time data triggers sirens and preemptive evacuations long before the flood hits living rooms Wetlands Protection The city is pushing for stricter zoning laws to protect remaining natural wetlands and ponding areas from being paved over by commercial developers allowing nature to absorb some of the rainwater According to local environmental groups like the Interface Development Intervention for Sustainability IDIS Davao City has lost a staggering 95 percent of its natural wetlands since 1945 due to rapid unchecked urban development Many of today's worst flood zones used to be natural swamps and marshes that absorbed rainwater As an alternative to concrete dams the LGU can focus on Nature-based Solutions NbS This includes legally protecting

text: Time to act AGUSAN BASIN DAVAO FLOODS SIGNS OF IMPENDING DISASTER By Manny Piñol In October of 2016 President Rody Duterte visited the typhoon devastated Cagayan Valley Region he warned that unless the mighty Cagayan River is dredged soon a disaster could happen inn the low-lying towns along the country's longest river The President said that soil erosion in the denuded mountains of the region ravaged by illegal logging operations have resulted in the heavy siltation of the meandering river causing it to overflow every time the rainy season or typhoons come The President's grim warning came true last week not in Cagayan Valley but at least five areas in Mindanao where soil erosion from bald mountains have caused heavy siltation and flash floods Flash floods and inundations occurred in Cagayan de Oro and Misamis Oriental Bukidnon the Cotabato River Basin Davao Region and the Agusan River Basin As heavy rains brought by the Tail-End of the Cold Front TECF poured in the mountains of these areas floodwaters rushed down causing rivers to overflow destroying crops and properties Hardest hit was the Agusan River Basin area which stretches from the mountains of Davao where mining and logging operations destroyed the forest cover to Butuan City up north Floods turned thousands of hectares of farmlands into a virtual sea affecting thousands of farming families When I visited the flood-hit areas and consulted with local leaders Thursday and Friday local leaders and stakeholders agreed that unless something is done fast a disaster worse than what these areas are suffering from now could happen anytime Aside from the emergency relief and rehabilitation efforts to be implemented by government there are at least two very important measures which must be started un the Duterte Presidency First dredging operations in the heavily silted rivers of the different river basins in the country especially Agusan River the Rio Grande de Mindanao in the Cotabato River Basin the Salog River in the Davao Region and the Cagayan River Second a well-coordinated national program to protect the remaining forests and reforest the denuded mountains must be done The Dept of Environment and Natural Resources DENR cannot do it alone and through the years it has been proven that its costly reforestation programs were monumental failures Under President Duterte who profoundly understands the impact of environmental depredation on agriculture and the lives of people these difficult tasks could be done President Duterte has shown in the past that he has the political will do protect the environment when he banned mining in Davao City This is where President Duterte's Iron-Hand leadership style is needed Leaders of Davao Provinces and Agusan del Sur have already agreed to convene the Agusan River Basin Management Council to address these problems I have asked them to submit within two weeks the things that need to be done to prevent the occurrence of another disastrous flood As soon as I get their recommendations I will immediately submit these to President Duterte These things must be done now Tomorrow will be too late Changeishere Pres Rody Cares Duterte Delivers Protect The Mountains First photo shows a submerged house in Barangay Nueva Era Bunawan Agusan del Sur second photo shows flooded rice fields in Carmen Davao del Norte and third photo shows the meandering and heavily-silted Cagayan River Photos by Al Jacalan John Pagaduan and Romirose Boloron

text: PROCLAMATION NO 5 Series of 2024 DECLARING THE SUSPENSION OF CLASSES IN ALL LEVELS OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS AND THE ADOPTION OF WORK-FROM-HOME ARRANGEMENT IN GOVERNMENT OFFICES IN DAVAO CITY ON THURSDAY FEBRUARY 1 2024 DUE TO HEAVY RAINS BROUGHT ABOUT BY THE TROUGH OF A LOW PRESSURE AREA WHEREAS at 5:00 PM of January 31 2024 the Department of Science and Technology Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration DOST-PAGASA issued Heavy Rainfall Warning Number 20 due to the trough of a low pressure area LPA continuing to affect areas in Mindanao WHEREAS the same advisory placed Davao City under the Red Warning Level more than 150,000 drums/square kilometer indicating that serious flooding is expected in low-lying areas and landslides are expected in mountainous areas WHEREAS at 2:30 PM of January 31 2024 the DOST-PAGASA Davao River Basin Flood Forecasting and Warning Center Regional Services Division-Mindanao issued Flood Advisory No 1 A on the Davao River Basin which forecasts scattered light to moderate with at times heavy rains within the next 24 hours in Davao City WHEREAS the same advisory indicates that the Davao River and its tributaries particularly Salug Matupe Kiulom Tagaulay Sita Dumalogdog Simud Ipuan Gumitan Upian Kulafu Suawan Siao and Tamugan Rivers are areas of concern with the water level in various parts of the Davao River currently at the alert and critical levels and still increasing WHEREAS with the continued moderate to heavy rainfall in the city causing increasing water levels at various rivers and flooding in certain streets the Davao City Disaster Risk Reduction Davao City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office has called for preemptive and mandatory evacuations in many areas in the city WHEREAS the City Government of Davao is duty-bound to safeguard the welfare of the public and undertake measures to avert any untoward incidents or disasters that may be caused by the effects of said weather occurrence NOW THEREFORE I SEBASTIAN Z DUTERTE Mayor of the City of Davao by virtue of the powers vested in me by law do hereby declare the following to take effect on Thursday February 1 2024:1 That classes and school activities in ALL LEVELS in all public and private educational institutions in Davao City are hereby suspended 2 That the Work-From-Home WFH arrangement shall be adopted in all national and local government offices including government-owned and controlled corporations in Davao City EXCEPT for offices performing safety and security health social services and disaster and emergency response services and 3 That private offices and establishments are given the discretion to suspend work or adopt WFH arrangements but are encouraged to do so for the safety and convenience of their employees Done this 31st day of January 2024 in Davao City Philippines

text: DAVAO'S FLOOD DEFENSES EXPLAINED How Retarding Ponds Cut-Off Channels and Dredging Work When millions of cubic meters of water pour down from upstream mountain catchments into the Davao Talomo and Matina River Basins how do we protect our communities from being submerged The insights and data shared here are not my own-they are drawn directly from the official DPWH-JICA Flood Control Master Plan In Part 1 we broke down why different neighborhoods face completely different flood risks Today in PART 2 we take a deep dive into the 4 major hard engineering solutions designed under this master plan to store accelerate and safely convey extreme 100 year flood waters out to sea 1 PRIORITY RETARDING PONDS Temporary Storage Upstream Affected Downstream Areas Callawa Mandug Waan Tigatto Ma-a Bucana Talomo Proper Matina Crossing and Matina Aplaya How It Works Think of these as massive engineered overflow reservoirs During heavy storms river channels quickly fill up Retarding ponds capture the peak flood surge upstream holding the excess water back until river levels safely drop The Engineering Specs Davao River RP 08 Callawa New Valencia 3.5 Million m3 capacity Davao River RP 09 Upper Callawa Bend 2.1 Million m3 capacity Davao River RP 11 Mandug New Carmen 4.8 Million m3 capacity Talomo River Basin Multi-site retention ponds covering approximately 4.8 million m2 to absorb excess volume before it hits downtown Matina River Basin A network of 12 critical offline/online ponds Ponds 8-10 13-18 23-25 strategically distributed to capture and cut peak flood discharge by 200 m3 s Combined Impact Over 10.4 MILLION cubic meters of temporary flood storage for the Davao River alone plus massive secondary retention across Talomo and Matina-the equivalent of thousands of Olympic-sized swimming pools held back from swamping the city 2 CUT-OFF CHANNELS COC Straightening Extreme River Bends Affected Areas Callawa New Valencia Ma-a Riverfront Area plus localized bottlenecks in Matina and Talomo How It Works Natural winding river loops slow down water velocity forcing floodwaters to pile up and breach their banks Cut-off channels construct straight bypass canals directly across narrow meander necks The Engineering Specs The 1.8 km Callawa Cut-Off Channel speeds up water flow dramatically dropping peak flood levels upstream and relieving severe hydraulic pressure on tight river bends Additionally short-term cut-off channel works are programmed for the winding sections of the Matina and Talomo rivers to prevent backwater piling and safely accelerate flow toward the coast 3 CHANNEL WIDENING and DREDGING Reclaiming River Capacity Affected Areas Ma-a Tigatto Bankerohan Barangay 19 Bucana Matina Crossing and Talomo Urban Center How It Works Decades of mountain erosion have washed tons of silt onto the riverbed choking its flow capacity while dense urban build-up has dangerously narrowed the natural waterways The Engineering Specs Deep channel dredging and excavation along critical downstream reaches of the Davao River lower the riverbed profile-expanding cross-sectional flow area so the river can carry higher discharge volumes In the Matina River the channel will be physically widened by an average of 6 meters 3m on each bank and 6 restrictive hydraulic bottleneck bridges will be replaced This massive upgrade will more than double Matina's flow capacity from a dangerous 150 m3 s up to a safe 350 m3 s 4 FLOODWALLS DIKES and REVETMENTS Wall-to-Wall Protection Affected Areas Densely populated urban barangays along the Davao Talomo and Matina river corridors How It Works Where urban density prevents widening the river lateral structures contain the water within the channel Raised concrete dikes prevent overflow while heavy reinforced concrete revetments absorb raging currents to prevent riverbank collapse The Engineering Specs Alongside the massive dikes for the main Davao River and drainage integration at the MacArthur Highway corridor in Talomo the highly vulnerable Matina River urban stretch will receive heavy reinforcements New concrete floodwalls here will average 2.6 meters high-reaching up to a towering 5.4 meters in critical spots including freeboard to securely contain the raging 100 year flood volumes THE TAKEAWAY SYSTEM INTEGRATION IS KEY No single dike or dredging project can solve Davao City's flood challenges alone Retarding ponds hold back the surge upstream Cut-Off Channels speed up flow past tight meanders and downstream widening dredging and dikes safely guide the water out to the Davao Gulf DAVAO FLOOD CONTROL SERIES 4 PART DEEP DIVE Read Part 1 Davao Flood Map Explained PART 2 Hard Engineering Interventions You Are Here NEXT UP PART 3 Non-Structural Measures Early Warning Telemetry Floodplain Zoni

text: On October 26 2024 a Community-Based Early Warning System and Flood Preparedness Orientation was held for the residents of Purok 11 and Purok 12 in Barangay Matina Pangi Davao City led by Engr Edwin G Patalagsa with assistance from our Chapter Based RC143 Volunteers namely Yñigo Monseda and Juanito Reasol The orientation was organized to address the unique flood risks in the area with a total of 51 participants including 25 Ateneo de Davao University AdDU NSTP students as part of their community engagement program The orientation aimed to equip community leaders and members with essential knowledge and strategies for flood preparedness introducing community-based early warning systems for flood-prone areas Moreover with the participation of Ateneo de Davao University NSTP students highlighted the importance of community involvement educating them in enhancing readiness and response and fostering disaster resilience in communities Keeping Humanity Alive

text: IT WAS MORE THAN A PUNCH By Truth Stream The rain did not arrive with a warning loud enough to stir panic It came like countless other rainy nights in Davao City Steady familiar almost ordinary Dabawenyos tucked their children into bed believing morning would come as it always had But somewhere in the darkness the waters were already gathering strength silently preparing to rewrite the lives of an entire community Before dawn broke on June 30 2011 Matina Pangi had become the epicenter of one of Davao City's deadliest flash floods In a matter of minutes homes were swallowed by a raging torrent Parents desperately searched for their children Neighbors risked their own lives to save strangers When the floodwaters finally receded they left behind more than shattered houses and mud-covered streets They left empty cradles unfinished dreams and a city mourning the loss of more than thirty lives most of them children Mayor Inday Sara Duterte then only 33 years old and herself a young mother woke up to a city devastated by tragedy One infant was never found Entire families were caught in total darkness as floodwaters engulfed their homes Some survived only by climbing trees while others escaped to the Matina Pangi Bridge carrying nothing but the clothes on their backs and the cellphones they managed to save As daylight broke the full extent of the catastrophe emerged lifeless bodies waiting to be recovered children still missing families desperately searching for loved ones and survivors left with nothing but mud where their homes once stood For Mayor Sara there was no time to grieve She immediately led relief operations visited evacuation centers comforted bereaved families and coordinated rescue and emergency response efforts Sleep and rest had to wait Yet before the city could even begin to recover from one tragedy another crisis erupted A court-ordered demolition in Agdao was set to proceed despite the city's standing policy that no demolition should take place unless affected residents had first been relocated Knowing the emotional state of the people after the flash flood Mayor Sara appealed to the court sheriff for just one or two hours so she could personally speak with the residents Her request was neither unreasonable nor defiant She simply wanted to prevent panic violence and the possibility of more people getting hurt Barely twenty-four hours had passed since more than thirty lives most of them children had been lost She did not want another tragedy unfolding in another part of the city Her plea was ignored While she was still in Matina attending to flood victims she learned that the demolition had already begun She rushed to Agdao wearing a light blue shirt and her signature short hair where television cameras were already rolling She motioned for the sheriff to come closer Seconds later she threw the punch that would become one of the most replayed political images in recent Philippine history Across the country many saw only a mayor punching a court officer What many never saw was the context he grief exhaustion and emotional weight of the previous twenty-four hours They did not see the flood victims she had just come from the parents searching for missing children or the families she had spent the day consoling The image of the punch became the story while everything that led to it slowly faded from public memory Mayor Sara later ensured that the sheriff received medical treatment publicly expressed regret over what had happened and in time both of them moved on from the incident Fifteen years later however that single moment was once again thrust into the national spotlight during the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte where prosecutors cited it as evidence of an alleged pattern of violent behavior For many Dabawenyos though the hearing revived a different memory They remembered the flood before they remembered the punch They remembered the children who died the families who lost everything and the young mayor who spent every waking hour responding to one of the darkest days in the city's history before rushing to stop what she believed could become another human tragedy As old footage resurfaced so did countless personal stories from Dabawenyos whose admiration for the Dutertes had been shaped not by political slogans but by lived experience Whether one agrees with Sara Duterte's actions that day or not history is rarely captured in a single frame Sometimes what appears to be a single punch is only the final chapter of a much longer story One written in floodwaters grief impossible decisions and a leader's fierce determination to stand with her people Perhaps that is why fifteen years later Dabawenyos continue to tell the story differently They remember not only the punch They remember everything that came before it VP Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial vpsaraimpeach

text: Update on the Nor'easter The rare early-season fall nor'easter is at its height bringing severe wind gusts heavy rain and coastal flooding risks to Boston's coastal and inland communities Tree and Wire Damage On Friday strong winds toppled a very large tree on Doone Avenue in Dorchester The falling tree took down power lines completely blocking off part of the street Dorchester police closed the area while utility and emergency crews worked on cleanup Elevated Outage Risk Because this storm has arrived unusually early in autumn many trees still have full foliage The combination of rain-soaked leaves and wind gusts up to 50-60 mph creates a much higher risk for downed branches and power outages across Dorchester Active Warnings and Key Forecast Details Peak Storm Window Today Saturday marks the absolute height of the storm Weather models show the system is retrograding reversing course back west which means it will linger much longer than a typical nor'easter with impacts potentially extending through Monday or Tuesday Flooding Concerns A Coastal Flood Warning is in place High northeast winds are continuously pushing water up against the shoreline making low-lying coastal areas in Dorchester vulnerable to tidal flooding The storm is expected to drop 2 to 4 inches of rain in total City Advisory and Reporting Info Boston Mayor Michelle Wu has urged residents to stay off the roads avoid unnecessary travel and never drive or wade through floodwaters To report emergencies or downed power lines immediately call 911 To report non-emergencies such as standard fallen trees street flooding or sewer backups use the Boston 311 app or call 311 BNA says stay safe Boston As the nor'easter peaks today please avoid unnecessary travel watch out for downed power lines and never drive through flooded roads
